alt: The Apple iPhone Duo foldable phone shown both folded and open, with the Touch ID fingerprint sensor and Camera Control button visible only on the right side of the device
story: Apple's first foldable iPhone, the Duo, launched September 9 at $1,999, but its Touch ID fingerprint sensor and Camera Control button sit exclusively on the right edge — the same right-biased design that sparked antennagate in 2010 — leaving the 10.6% of users who are left-handed unable to comfortably unlock or shoot photos on a phone Apple markets as its most ambitious ever.
why_funny: After Steve Jobs' infamous 'you're holding it wrong' response in 2010, Apple spent 16 years and released a $2,000 foldable phone that once again asks left-handed users to hold it differently.
